author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Map an Xbox-style controller for PS2 games
summary: Create a clean Port 1 profile by mapping PS2 functions from physical positions, testing both analog sticks, triggers, stick clicks, Start and Select, and proving one press produces one intended input after reconnect.
heroAlt: PCSX2 global controller settings with SDL input source and automatic mapping controls

sourceLabels.android-game-controller: Android controller events, axes, and device behavior

blocks.text: Map PS2 functions from position, not printed letters

Xbox-style A, B, X, and Y labels do not match the PlayStation symbol names shown by PS2 games. Begin with one controller and a blank or known-good profile. Bind the south, east, west, and north physical buttons to Cross, Circle, Square, and Triangle by position, then assign shoulders, analog triggers, stick axes, stick clicks, D-pad, Start, and Select. Keep the device connected in one Android mode throughout the procedure.
Do not map the same physical button through both automatic mapping and a second manual entry. Duplicate bindings can make menus move twice or activate two PS2 controls at once.

items: Controller paired or connected and visible to Android before EmuCoreX starts.
Only one gamepad active while the base profile is created.
Existing working mapping exported or photographed.
A PS2 title with menus plus analog movement available for verification.
Controller firmware and Android mode left unchanged during mapping.

blocks.text: Build Port 1 in a fixed order

items: 1. Open the Port 1 mapping and clear only accidental or unknown bindings.
2. Bind D-pad directions and verify each returns to neutral.
3. Bind face buttons by physical position to the four PS2 symbols.
4. Assign L1, R1, L2, R2, L3, R3, Start, and Select individually.
5. Move each stick through X and Y while watching direction and full range.
6. Inspect the profile for repeated physical codes before saving.
7. Cold-boot the test game and check menus, gameplay, and simultaneous stick-plus-button input.
8. Disconnect, reconnect, restart the app, and repeat the critical controls.

blocks.text: Mapping by physical position preserves the layout expected by PS2 software even when the shell uses different letters. A reconnect test catches profiles bound to a transient device instance. Testing simultaneous input exposes conflicts that a simple menu cannot reveal.
Every physical control must reach exactly one intended PS2 input and remain stable after reconnection.

items: One button press advances one menu item or action.
Both sticks reach cardinal and diagonal directions without drift.
L2 and R2 reach released and fully pressed states.
Start, Select, L3, and R3 work in their intended contexts.
The profile remains assigned to Port 1 after app restart.
Face buttons feel swapped: remap by position rather than label.
Menus jump twice: remove duplicate automatic or manual entries.
One trigger acts as an axis and button: keep only the intended binding.
Reconnect changes the device: rebuild a device-specific profile after confirming Android mode.

blocks.text: Import the saved mapping or restore the photographed assignments, remove the failed device-specific profile, and restart with one controller connected. Do not reset unrelated touchscreen or Port 2 settings.
Android controller modes can expose different codes

Some pads offer XInput-like, Android, DirectInput, or Switch modes. Changing that switch creates a different logical device and may invalidate mappings even though the physical controller is unchanged. Record the mode beside the profile name and retest both sticks plus triggers after firmware updates or re-pairing. If Android exposes the pad as a keyboard in one mode, do not merge those codes into the working gamepad profile; return to the verified mode and preserve one clean device identity.
